name: What is the difference between a recurring drain clog and a one-time clog?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a recurring drain clog and a one-time clog?

acceptedAnswer.text: A one-time clog is typically an isolated incident, often resolved with basic methods like plunging. A recurring clog, however, indicates a persistent underlying issue. This could be a significant blockage accumulating over time, pipe damage, or a structural problem in your plumbing system that continuously hinders water flow. Recurring clogs require professional diagnosis and often more advanced solutions than simple household remedies.
acceptedAnswer.description: A one-time clog is an isolated event, while a recurring clog suggests an underlying, persistent plumbing issue requiring professional assessment.
